claims.status_note: #2 answers that holders are already diluted without control to fund miners (88% of the subsidy); #31 and #62 add that coinholder voting also overrides minorities and the wider community. No asserter conceded.
claims.text: ZCG spends coinholder money, taken through dilution every block, without coinholders controlling it; the people who pay have no say while the people who get paid (ZCAP members, ZCG grantees) do, which is a moral hazard.

claims.status_note: #14 says ZCAP eligibility has many routes, #64 says the figures alone do not prove improper decisions, and #125 says the one grantee panelist named, Hanh, is neutral in the meeting minutes.
claims.text: ZCAP, which elects ZCG, includes many ZCG grantees (72 of about 200 members, 36%, behind about 75% of ZCG payouts), so ZCAP/ZCG is an insular body that votes itself money and ZCG is a self-serving organisation.

claims.status_note: #58 and #60 say the ZSA decision rests on a 2022 community document and #126 says ZCG never funded sex work itself. #66 later yielded the ZSA point, but #59 and #61 hold that the wider pattern stands.
claims.text: ZCG repeatedly funds things coinholders oppose: coinholders voted 98.6% against Zcash Shielded Assets (ZCAP 70.4% for), ZCG approved another $455K for ZSAs in June, and it also funded adult-event outreach.

claims.status_note: #133 answers that capital allocation needs smart people rather than thousands, and that ZCG should take time to adjust to its larger budget. No one else addressed the argument directly.
claims.text: Committees cannot know what to fund: the knowledge needed to allocate well is spread across many users and builders and shows up in what people choose to pay for, so any five people would face the same problem.

claims.status_note: Rebuttals say private money is unreliable, investor-controlled and not available at scale (#28, #53, #100, #115) and #24 calls loans and VC non-cypherpunk. #35 asked for three funders; no reply names any.
claims.text: Donors, companies and crowdfunding can fill the gaps if ZCG ends, as in Bitcoin and Linux, and Zcash's biggest work is already privately funded; some community and non-core projects would go unfunded.

claims.status_note: #15 says the NSM exists anyway, is the path of least resistance and that not paying miners was not the goal; #23 prefers money to miners securing the network over ZCG grants. Neither denies the effect described.
claims.text: Ending ZCG without replacing its 8% with another development-oriented stream, or sending it to the NSM (which starts paying out only in 2031), amounts to giving more money to miners and less to development and maintenance.

claims.status_note: #12 argues that if dev funding is no longer needed the whole fund should be retired and #1 says private funding already carries the biggest work; #21 and #36 want the dev fund ended outright. #52 sees no sign it is no longer needed.
claims.text: Ongoing protocol-level development funding is still needed (critical infrastructure, security work, bug bounties) and Zcash should keep it secured, including through bear markets, rather than retire it.

claims.status_note: #27, #32 and #64 argue votes may follow connections or concentrated capital and #103 calls it a whale oligarchy. #134 and #136 asked for evidence of maturity and of coinholders doing better than ZCG; no reply is in the thread.
claims.text: Coinholder voting has matured and works better than ZCG/ZCAP: holders vote on every grant, the work it funded (protocol, security, audits, bug bounties) has been high-signal, and it answers to the people who bear the cost.

claims.status_note: #81 replies that this is not a foregone conclusion and that coinholders could be convinced a ZCG-like structure has value. #74 accepts the prediction but asks how the community's wish should be measured.
claims.text: A coinholder vote or poll would overwhelmingly favour ending ZCG, as the ZSA vote did.

claims.status_note: #68 replies that Zcash left out UASF support, so a fork is not really possible.
claims.text: Abruptly dismissing ZCG without letting its members get something out of a deal would cause a revolt and possibly a fork, so a negotiated outcome is the better path.

claims.status_note: #18, #52 and #129 argue the coinholder stream is accountable and has funded security and infrastructure, so it should stay; #52 also disputes #12's premise that dev funding is no longer needed.
claims.text: ZCG and the coinholder-grants stream should be treated alike: if ZCG's funding ends, the 12% coinholder stream should end too (the whole dev fund), or neither should, and coinholder voting deserves the same scrutiny.

claims.status_note: #12 argues that killing only one part is a mistake and that a half measure leaves the door open to ongoing politics. No one else rebutted the call to unbundle.
claims.text: Ending the ZCG stream, stripping ZCG's existing treasury and ending the coinholder-grants stream should be separate proposals, so people can choose to end one, both or neither.

claims.status_note: #15 replies that the NSM already exists and will continue with or without ZCG's stream, and that its payout and conditions are subject to change anyway. It does not address the complexity point.
claims.text: Putting the funds in the NSM is problematic: the reserve could become a dev fund in waiting that is later redirected, and the NSM is a hard-to-explain second issuance curve that complicates Zcash's economics and story.

claims.status_note: #14 links the Foundation's ZCAP page. Nobody replied on ZCAP eligibility, and maxdesalle posted only #1 in the thread.
claims.text: Posting on the forum and receiving a ZCG grant are only two of many ways to be eligible for ZCAP, and presenting only those two is misleading.

claims.status_note: #122 says Monero and Bitcoin maxis will criticise Zcash whatever it does; #53 says Zcash does not need to win Bitcoiners over and that its funding stream is a strength.
claims.text: Block-reward grants run by a self-serving committee like ZCG do not belong in a network meant to be sound, fair money, and they hurt Zcash's credibility with Bitcoin and Monero advocates.

claims.status_note: #82 says ZCG receives the same ZEC as always and the debate should be about performance; #53 and #96 want the money deployed at scale. ZCG members hanh (#86) and artkor (#93) concede the size point; hanh opposes dissolution.
claims.text: The ZCG treasury has grown too large for any committee to allocate responsibly, regardless of its performance, so its funding stream should stop.

claims.status_note: #20 asked @ebfull and @joshs to confirm they were not among the recipients; nobody answered that question or #33's version of the point.
claims.text: Developers and others advocating coinholder voting have conflicts of interest, because Zcash already paid founders very large rewards (tens to hundreds of thousands of ZEC) and some benefited from Dev Fund personal grants.

claims.status_note: #98 objects to putting the money in a nonprofit foundation and proposes burning it; #100 argues against burning. artkor (#50) declined to give an opinion. No one else weighed the idea on its merits.
claims.text: ZCG's existing treasury should be converted into a fiat trust or formal nonprofit so it can fund development for years from interest without drawing further block rewards, and can fund university research directly.

claims.status_note: #23, #59, #61 and #121 point to the ZSA vote, adult-event funding and grants coinholders reject. #24 agrees ZSAs were a mistake and #66 later yielded that point, while keeping that ZCG is mostly conservative.
claims.text: ZCG has been conservative and careful, rejecting even small proposals, with only a handful of failures (three or four) among hundreds of funded proposals, so its record does not justify dissolving it.

claims.status_note: #11 says ebfull would personally support stripping ZCG's existing treasury, in a separate proposal; #1 and #6 propose sending the remainder to the NSM.
claims.text: ZCG's existing treasury should stay with ZCG, possibly converted into a trust; stopping new deposits is acceptable, but sending the accumulated funds to the NSM takes what ZCG holds.

claims.status_note: These are allegations about interest, not findings: maxdesalle disclosed Cypherpunk ties in #1 and posted nothing further. #56, #72 and #88 deny a conspiracy or hidden motive; #23 says ZCG's grants are worse even if it were true.
claims.text: The push to end ZCG is driven by miners and large holders (Cypherpunk, Winklevoss-linked investors, whales) who stand to gain from redirecting block rewards, and it centralises Zcash.

claims.status_note: #76 says Frank's concern was low participation and bad voting UI and sees no sign coinholder grants caused the problems ZCAP did; #52 says retroactive grants funded infrastructure and security. #64 adds that vulnerability is not proven abuse.
claims.text: Coinholder voting has accountability problems: votes are anonymous and may not be informed, large capital can sway outcomes, and results may follow connections rather than merit (a 17-user project won 1.5M votes; a $4,000 request failed).

claims.status_note: #1 says private funding already carries Tachyon, Valar and ZODL and that donors and retroactive coinholder grants can fill gaps; #33 grants that some community projects would go unfunded.
claims.text: Relying on private investors is unreliable and gives them control: they can withdraw funding or dictate what is built, will not fund Zcash at the scale of a foundation, and force small builders to front costs or give up equity.

claims.status_note: Nobody replied to the macro-timing argument; later posts dispute the pace of the process instead.
claims.text: The timing is wrong: structural change should not be rushed in a credit crunch on the eve of a financial crisis, when liquidity will evaporate and funding will become scarce.

claims.status_note: #4 and #5 reply that people with skin in the game, miners and coinholders, should hold control; #5 admits early pioneers with reputation but few coins may object and does not say how to resolve it.
claims.text: Large coinholders should not be the sole decision-makers on funding: holders by count, the wider community and developers deserve a voice, and majority or whale voting still dilutes those who do not want a project.

claims.status_note: artkor put it conditionally ('if we see truly broad support'). Nobody replied.
claims.text: Even if ZCG ends, a reserve such as the Lockbox should be kept, because nobody knows what the future holds and giving up a reserve would be overconfident.

claims.status_note: #45 acknowledges ZCG had a few weeks' heads-up. #63 and #89 dispute the framing and say a public discussion should have come first; no ZCG member denied the no vote or the silence.
claims.text: ebfull says ZCG agreed in September that its treasury was out of control, voted no on a voluntary lockbox, said it would start a public discussion but stayed silent through October, and misled him in private communications.

claims.status_note: #83 replies that no single organisation can efficiently and responsibly allocate such an enormous amount of capital when it was never designed for that purpose.
claims.text: Zcash should deploy its enlarged treasury aggressively (marketing, events, full-time hires, onboarding ordinary users, DeFi growth) under experienced nonprofit leadership, rather than retreat from community funding.

claims.status_note: Raised in #53; nobody replied to it.
claims.text: Removing community funding is anti-competitive: organisations that relied on grants for years now oppose community funding because they are financially comfortable.

claims.status_note: #51 and #83 say they lost faith in ZCG and would favour shutting it down for reasons beyond treasury size; #1 argues any five people would face the same problem.
claims.text: ZCG should be restructured rather than abolished, for example with sub-committees and grant tracks, experienced full-time or nonprofit leadership, clearer goals and better-aligned incentives.

claims.status_note: #59 and #61 say the coinholder vote, not the earlier document, is what matters. The asserter of #58 and #60 then yielded the ZSA point in #66, saying ZCG was in a sunk-cost fallacy.
claims.text: The ZSA program rested on a community consensus document from 2022 with named signers, so ZCG's ZSA funding is not recent evidence of overriding coinholders.

claims.status_note: #16 and #121 say the objection is to funding sex events or sex work from block rewards, which they call out of touch; #126 replies that the grant bought a marketing presence at adult expos, not sex work.
claims.text: Funding Zcash outreach at adult-industry events and to at-risk groups such as sex workers is a legitimate marketing use of grants, because Zcash protects at-risk people; ZCG did not fund sex work itself.

claims.status_note: #91 and #51 reply that the treasury accumulates millions weekly, ZCG had all of October, and delay worsens it; #95 says it was ZCG's job to propose a solution.
claims.text: The process is too fast for a legitimate decision: weeks are too few for a structural change, ordinary coinholders and ZCG members only just learned of it, and an interim pledge to hold new funds would remove any urgency.

claims.status_note: #100 says burning shrinks supply for dominant holders and leaves developers reliant on investors; #110 says random deflation is no better than inflation. No one else endorsed it.
claims.text: Burning the ZCG-held ZEC forever would be more useful than placing it in a nonprofit foundation.

claims.status_note: strahncryptography softened in #112 and #114 after artkor and thowar2 explained the model, accepting Zcash Labs as a complement to ZCG. He did not withdraw the objection to it replacing ZCG.
claims.text: Zcash Labs fronts money for projects and then asks coinholders to reimburse it plus a 20% markup; thowar2 therefore stands to gain from replacing ZCG with coinholder voting, which is a conflict of interest.

claims.status_note: #103 says this is the whale-oligarchy problem personified and #107 says exchange wallets could take over with no reputational risk, turning it into a corporate oligarchy.
claims.text: A committee of the largest Zcash holders who choose to disclose their holdings could replace ZCG, because they would risk their reputations and could not hide behind sockpuppets.

claims.status_note: #100 and #105 compare it to a16z or Paradigm and call it a VC or arbitrage; #113 answers the comparison point by point. #110 defends a premium for upfront risk.
claims.text: Zcash Labs is not a VC: it spends its own money, takes no equity or upside, and is reimbursed (cost plus 20%) only if coinholders vote for a project, the inverse of venture capital, which keeps it accountable for value.

claims.status_note: #118 replies that ZCG holds someone else's money and so can never be indiscriminate; #119 answers that fiduciary duty bars recklessness but does not cap spending.
claims.text: A grants program exists to take chances on speculative or unpalatable work that private investors will not back, so ZCG's mandate to fund such work, and its freedom with the funds it holds, is the reason it exists.

claims.status_note: #116 asks what is wrong with competing and says the better model should win; #117 replies that only ZCG can authorise unprofitable or unpalatable work.
claims.text: Zcash Labs-style commercial funding complements ZCG rather than competing with it, because ZCG funds work that cannot be monetised, such as research and community building, while Labs funds ventures with commercial prospects.

claims.status_note: Raised by zcashminer1 as a structural rather than personal critique; nobody replied.
claims.text: ZCG is passive by design and has no defined goals, so it can only fund what is brought to it, success cannot be measured, and stakeholders hold it to conflicting standards.

claims.status_note: artkor cites a tweet as evidence of the plan (#138). Nobody replied; later posts move to Crosslink.
claims.text: Ending ZCG is the first step of a multi-step plan to shut down the Lockbox, delegitimise ZCAP decisions and give miners and large holders sole control of funding.

claims.status_note: #141 replies that wallets may favour the biggest finalisers, who are current miners, so staking could turn into a cartel. Both posts are side-topics to the ZCG question.
claims.text: PoW mining operations centralise and become easier to attack, so redundancy such as Crosslink is not optional.

mind_changes.note: Yields the ZSA point after #59 and #61, accepting ZCG was in a sunk-cost fallacy, while still arguing for restructuring over abolition.
mind_changes.span: also yield to you on the ZSA point: ZCG was clearly in a sunk-cost fallacy dilemma, aiming to fulfill a grant that they had sunk millions in, not willing to immediately abandon it.

mind_changes.note: After Shawn's #74, a ZCG member says funds must adapt; he does not say whether he supports the proposal.
mind_changes.span: Funds must adapt to the new conditions.

mind_changes.note: A ZCG member accepts the argument, made in #74 and #83, that ZCG cannot handle these volumes.
mind_changes.span: I also completely agree with the argument that ZCG will never be able to handle these volumes.

mind_changes.note: After artkor's #111, moves from criticising Zcash Labs to supporting it as a complement to ZCG, not a replacement.
mind_changes.span: now I see your point. In that respect, yes, I can support Zcash Labs too

mind_changes.note: After thowar2's #113, says he understands the model and sees its merits if it does not compete with ZCG.
mind_changes.span: Yes, I understand the model now. As long as it's not competing with ZCG, I see its merits

open_questions.text: By what mechanism can the community's wish about ZCG and its funds be determined, given that a coinholder poll and a ZCAP poll would each be disputed?
Should ZCG's existing treasury be redirected to the NSM, or stay with ZCG (possibly as a trust), when ebfull says stopping the stream and stripping the treasury should be separate proposals?
If ZCG's stream ends, what accountable mechanism funds critical protocol work, and who funds non-core community projects?
What evidence shows coinholder voting is more reliable than ZCG, and how would whale influence and anonymous votes be handled? Requests for evidence went unanswered.
Will ZCG publish its own plan for its treasury, which ebfull says it promised, and what is its response to the proposal?
Were the founders and developers advocating the change among recipients of the large founders' rewards, as strahncryptography asked of ebfull and joshs?

overview.text: maxdesalle opens by proposing that ZCG stop approving grants at NU8 and that its 8% share and remaining treasury go to the NSM, arguing that coinholders pay but do not control ZCG, that ZCG spends against their votes, and that committees cannot know what to fund (#1). Several posters give full support (#3, #4, #5, #7), while str4d warns that without a replacement stream this shifts money from development to miners (#2) and secparam objects to the NSM as a destination (#13), which ebfull defends as the existing path of least resistance (#15).

The proposal splits quickly over scope. ebfull files a draft ZIP stopping only the ZCG stream and wants separate proposals (#11); joshs says half measures are a mistake and drafts a ZIP ending the whole dev fund (#6, #12); thailand85 and Monsignoree agree both should go, though thailand85 wants separate votes (#14, #17, #36); Umbredak, thowar2 and ACoffee defend the coinholder stream (#18, #52, #129). Batuhan and Milton argue coinholder voting has the same flaws and deserves the same scrutiny (#27, #31, #32, #64).

Participants dispute whether private funding can replace grants (#28, #33, #35, #53, #100) and whether ZCG's record is careful (#20, #58, #105) or marked by decisions against coinholders such as ZSAs and adult-event funding (#23, #59, #61, #121; defended in #62, #126, #128). Interest allegations run both ways: that backers profit as miners (#22, #45, #55, #138) and that developers, Zcash Labs or ebfull have conflicts (#20, #70, #100).

ZCG members join from #41. ebfull describes a September lockbox offer ZCG declined and a silent October (#51, #91, #95), while artkor and others reply about process, tone and motives (#45, #54, #63, #89). Calls to cool the thread come from seernet and emersonian (#56, #87), though some posts turn personal (#69, #98, #123). Shawn, hanh and artkor accept that the treasury has outgrown ZCG's management (#74, #86, #93).

A long side exchange on Zcash Labs' cost-plus retroactive model ends with strahncryptography accepting it as a complement to ZCG (#100, #104, #111, #112, #113, #114). Others propose reforming or professionalising ZCG, converting it to a fiat trust or nonprofit, or replacing it with a committee of disclosed top holders (#53, #94, #96, #97, #102, #103, #115, #137).

Later posts add zcashminer1's and common1's case for fixing ZCG rather than ending it (#133, #137), artkor's claim of a multi-step plan to take over funding (#138, #139), and brief support (#129, #130, #131, #143). The thread records no vote or ZCG decision, and Shawn's question of how to measure the community's wishes (#74) is unanswered.

positions.label: End ZCG and move its funds to the NSM, keeping Coinholder grants
positions.summary: Coinholders fund ZCG through dilution but cannot control it, ZCAP includes many grantees, ZCG has spent against coinholder votes such as the ZSA vote, and mature coinholder voting is the accountable alternative. Private funding and retroactive grants can carry development.

positions.label: End the whole dev fund, ZCG and Coinholder grants together
positions.summary: Half measures leave the door open to ongoing debate and politics; coinholder grants were a bridge when funding was scarce and have served their purpose; one cannot end ZCG and keep the other stream. thailand85 would vote to end both but wants separate votes.

positions.label: Stop ZCG's stream now because its treasury is too large
positions.summary: The ZCG treasury has grown beyond what any committee was designed to handle, regardless of performance, so the stream should stop in a separate proposal; ZCG had October to propose its own solution and did not. hanh agrees on the size but not on dissolving ZCG.

positions.label: Apply the same scrutiny to Coinholder voting, or remove both
positions.summary: Coinholder votes are anonymous, may be uninformed and can be swayed by capital or connections, so questioning only ZCG's accountability is inconsistent. Remove both or neither, and fix the weaknesses of each system.

positions.label: Reform or professionalise ZCG instead of abolishing it
positions.summary: ZCG has been careful and its failures few; the real problems are structure, scale, goals and incentives. Options include sub-committees and grant tracks, experienced nonprofit leadership, a fiat trust or nonprofit, and putting the capital to work for growth.

positions.label: The NSM mainly benefits miners; development funding needs a home
positions.summary: Ending ZCG's stream without a development-oriented replacement, or sending it to an NSM that pays from 2031, shifts money to miners; the NSM is also complex and could be redirected. Dev funding must stay secured.

positions.label: Backers act in the interests of miners and large holders
positions.summary: The proposal's promoters stand to gain through mining (Cypherpunk, Winklevoss-linked investors, whales); ending ZCG centralises Zcash and is a step toward taking over funding. Some also allege conflicts for named participants.

summary.tldr: Proposal to end ZCG's 8% funding stream and send its funds to the NSM. Backers cite coinholders' lack of control and ZCG spending against their votes; critics defend ZCG's record, want reform, or question backers' motives and Coinholder voting. Treasury size and scope of cuts remain unresolved.
